recipes.title: Oyakodon, light
recipes.summary: Tender chicken and softly set egg simmered with onion in a savoury Japanese sauce, served over a modest bowl of rice. It stays comforting while keeping the starch and sweetener restrained.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Slice the onion, chicken thigh and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar to a gentle simmer in a small pan.
Add the onion and simmer until it becomes soft and translucent.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until the thigh is opaque and cooked through.
Pour the eggs evenly over the chicken and cook gently until softly set but still moist.
Spoon the chicken and eggs over the white rice and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately while the eggs are soft. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently until steaming; add a spoonful of water if the rice seems dry.

recipes.title: Oyakodon
recipes.summary: Classic Japanese chicken and egg simmered with onion in a lightly sweet soy broth, spooned over warm rice. The eggs stay tender and bind the savoury sauce to every grain.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Slice the onion, chicken thigh and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar to a gentle simmer in a small pan.
Add the onion and simmer until soft and translucent.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until the thigh is cooked through and tender.
Pour the eggs evenly over the chicken and cook gently until softly set.
Spoon the chicken and eggs over the white rice and scatter over the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served straight away. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat gently until steaming throughout. The egg will firm on reheating, so avoid high heat.

recipes.title: Oyakodon, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Japanese bowl with extra chicken, rice and egg in a savoury-sweet onion broth. It is filling enough for a hungry lunch while keeping the familiar soft, comforting texture.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the larger portion finishes steaming evenly.
Slice the onion, chicken thigh and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar to a gentle simmer in a wide pan.
Add the onion and simmer until completely soft and translucent.
Add the chicken thigh and simmer until the thigh is opaque, tender and cooked through.
Pour the eggs evenly over the chicken and cook gently until the eggs are softly set.
Spoon the chicken and eggs over the white rice and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat gently until steaming. Add a splash of water before reheating if the rice has absorbed all the sauce.

recipes.title: Korean pork belly cabbage wraps, light
recipes.summary: Seared pork belly wrapped in crisp cabbage with garlic, cucumber and nutty sesame spring onions. Extra cabbage keeps the plate generous while the pork portion stays measured.

steps.instruction: Separate the green cabbage into broad leaves and trim any very thick ribs.
Slice the garlic, spring onions and cucumber into their prepared sizes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, then transfer them to a bowl.
Heat a grill pan and cook the pork belly in a single layer until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic to the pork belly and cook until fragrant and lightly golden.
Toss the spring onions with the sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds.
Rest the pork belly briefly so the juices settle.
Fill the green cabbage leaves with pork belly, cucumber and the spring onion mixture.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled at the table. Refrigerate cooked pork belly for up to 3 days and reheat until hot. Keep the cabbage, cucumber and sesame mixture separate so they stay crisp.

recipes.title: Korean pork belly cabbage wraps
recipes.summary: Golden pork belly served with crisp cabbage leaves, cucumber, garlic and sesame-seasoned spring onions. Each diner builds their own savoury Korean-style wrap at the table.

steps.instruction: Separate the green cabbage into broad leaves and trim the thickest ribs.
Slice the garlic, spring onions and cucumber into their prepared sizes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, then transfer them to a bowl.
Heat a grill pan and cook the pork belly in a single layer until deeply browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic to the pork belly and cook until lightly golden and fragrant.
Toss the spring onions with the sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds.
Rest the pork belly briefly so the juices settle.
Fill the green cabbage leaves with pork belly, cucumber and the spring onion mixture.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the cooked pork belly separately from the vegetables for up to 3 days. Reheat the pork until hot and assemble the cabbage wraps just before eating.

recipes.title: Korean pork belly cabbage wraps, hearty
recipes.summary: A plentiful platter of deeply browned pork belly with crisp cabbage, cucumber and sesame spring onions. The build-your-own wraps make a substantial, lively Korean dinner.

steps.instruction: Separate the green cabbage into broad leaves and trim the thickest ribs.
Slice the garlic, spring onions and cucumber into their prepared sizes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, then transfer them to a bowl.
Heat a grill pan and cook the pork belly in batches until deeply browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic to the final batch of pork belly and cook until lightly golden.
Toss the spring onions with the sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds.
Rest the pork belly briefly so the juices settle.
Fill the green cabbage leaves with pork belly, cucumber and the spring onion mixture.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate cooked pork belly for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot pan. Keep the cabbage, cucumber and sesame spring onions chilled and separate until serving.

recipes.title: Scandinavian smoked salmon open sandwiches, light
recipes.summary: Open sandwiches layered with smoked salmon, cucumber and a cool dill yogurt spread. The lighter version uses thinner bread and extra cucumber while keeping the salmon generous.

steps.instruction: Slice the cucumber and spring onions and arrange the bread on a board.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over the bread.
Layer the salmon and cucumber over each slice of bread.
Finish the open sandwiches with the spring onions and serve immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled just before eating. Refrigerate the salmon and yogurt spread separately for up to 2 days. Once assembled, the bread softens quickly and should not be frozen.

recipes.title: Scandinavian smoked salmon open sandwiches
recipes.summary: Nordic-style open sandwiches with smoked salmon, crisp cucumber and a tangy dill yogurt spread. They are cool, savoury and substantial enough for a shared snack.

steps.instruction: Slice the cucumber and spring onions and arrange the bread on a board.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth and spoonable.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over the bread.
Layer the salmon and cucumber generously over each slice of bread.
Scatter over the spring onions and serve the open sandwiches immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep the components refrigerated separately for up to 2 days and assemble shortly before serving. The finished sandwiches do not freeze well.

recipes.title: Scandinavian smoked salmon open sandwiches, hearty
recipes.summary: Generous open sandwiches piled with smoked salmon, cucumber and creamy dill yogurt. Extra bread and salmon make them a filling high-protein Nordic snack for two.

steps.instruction: Slice the cucumber and spring onions and arrange the bread on a large board.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth.
Spread the greek yogurt mixture evenly over all the bread.
Layer the salmon and cucumber generously over each slice of bread.
Finish with the spring onions and serve the open sandwiches immediately.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the bread at room temperature and refrigerate the remaining components separately for up to 2 days. Assemble only what will be eaten immediately.

recipes.title: Thai shrimp rice porridge, light
recipes.summary: A gentle Thai breakfast porridge with tender shrimp, ginger, garlic and fish sauce. Extra broth keeps it generous while the rice portion stays light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Bring the vegetable broth, ginger, garlic and fish sauce to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the grains are very soft and the broth looks lightly thickened.
Add the shrimp and simmer until the shrimp are pink and opaque.
Rest the porridge off the heat so the rice thickens slightly.
Divide the porridge between bowls and finish with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat until steaming, adding extra vegetable broth because the rice thickens as it stands. Do not freeze the finished porridge.

recipes.title: Thai shrimp rice porridge
recipes.summary: Comforting Thai rice porridge simmered until silky, with plump shrimp, ginger, garlic and fish sauce. Fresh herbs and lime brighten each warm bowl.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Bring the vegetable broth, ginger, garlic and fish sauce to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the grains begin to break down and the porridge turns silky.
Add the shrimp and simmer until the shrimp are pink and opaque throughout.
Rest the porridge off the heat so the rice thickens slightly.
Divide the porridge between bowls and finish with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate promptly for up to 2 days. Reheat gently with extra vegetable broth until steaming, as the rice absorbs liquid while stored. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Thai shrimp rice porridge, hearty
recipes.summary: A substantial Thai breakfast porridge with extra rice and shrimp, simmered with ginger, garlic and fish sauce. Cilantro, spring onions and lime keep the rich bowl fresh.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the ginger, garlic, spring onions, cilantro and lime.
Bring the vegetable broth, ginger, garlic and fish sauce to a gentle boil.
Add the white rice and simmer until the larger amount of rice is very soft and the porridge is thick.
Add the shrimp and simmer until the shrimp are pink, firm and opaque.
Rest the porridge off the heat so the rice settles into a creamy texture.
Divide the porridge between bowls and finish with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 2 days and reheat with enough vegetable broth to loosen the thickened rice. Heat until steaming throughout. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Turkish stuffed eggplant, light
recipes.summary: Roasted eggplant filled with savoury beef, onion, garlic and tomato. This lighter version uses less oil and beef while keeping the classic soft eggplant and rich filling.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Score the cut sides of the eggplant and brush them with half the olive oil.
Roast the eggplant until the flesh is soft and lightly browned.
Chop the onion and garlic while the eggplant roasts.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until the beef is browned and no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, canned, and tomato paste and simmer until the filling is thick.
Press a hollow into each roasted eggplant half and divide the beef filling between them.
Bake the stuffed eggplant until the filling is bubbling and the edges are tender.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until hot throughout. The stuffed eggplant can be frozen for up to 2 months, though the flesh will soften after thawing.

recipes.title: Turkish stuffed eggplant
recipes.summary: Tender roasted eggplant boats filled with beef, onion, garlic and a rich tomato sauce. Baking the filled eggplants brings the classic Turkish flavours together.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Score the cut sides of the eggplant and brush them with half the olive oil.
Roast the eggplant until the flesh is very soft and lightly browned.
Chop the onion and garlic while the eggplant roasts.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until the beef is browned and cooked through.
Stir in the tomatoes, canned, and tomato paste and simmer until the filling is rich and thick.
Press a hollow into each roasted eggplant half and divide the beef filling between them.
Bake the stuffed eggplant until the filling bubbles and the edges are tender.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat covered in the oven or microwave until steaming. Freeze portions for up to 2 months and thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: Turkish stuffed eggplant, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous tray of roasted eggplant packed with extra beef and a deeply savoury tomato filling. It makes a substantial Turkish keto lunch for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Score the cut sides of the eggplant and brush them with half the olive oil.
Roast the eggplant until the thick flesh is very soft and browned at the edges.
Chop the onion and garlic while the eggplant roasts.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until the beef is deeply browned and cooked through.
Stir in the tomatoes, canned, and tomato paste and simmer until the filling is thick and glossy.
Press a generous hollow into each roasted eggplant half and divide the beef filling between them.
Bake the stuffed eggplant until the filling is bubbling and the eggplant edges are tender.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until piping hot. Freeze individual stuffed eggplant halves for up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating.
